caption: The drawing consists of a symmetrical floral design composed of stylized flowers, leaves, and buds, predominantly rendered in shades of muted green, yellow, brownish red, and light tan. At the center is a large, abstract flower with a wide, maroon-red bowl-shaped base outlined in light green, filled with yellow segments, and topped with upward-pointing petals. Above this, a light green flame-like shape is decorated with clusters of circular dots in green and red. Flanking the central flower, two smaller stylized blossoms appear on both sides, each with six light green petals outlined in green, a yellow inner section, and a red circle at the center. These side flowers are supported by long, curving green stems that rise and twist outward, each ending in a yellow bud with a red accent and surrounded by blue-green leaves. Below the main flower, two additional smaller flowers are positioned symmetrically, each with yellow petals tipped with red, green stems, and curling green leaves. The drawing has a cream-colored background with some scattered black spots and is labeled with text at the bottom and top left corner, indicating it is a depiction of altar tabernacle decoration from San Luis Obispo Mission, in the style of Spanish California decorative art.
title: San Luis Obispo Mission Altar Tabernacle From the portfolio "Decorative Art of Spanish California"
